doc.title: David Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2022

title: Cecil McBee's role and what makes the Cookers a great band
summary: Weiss says Cecil McBee can keep steady time or roam, and compares the Cookers to great bands where members know their roles, like the Spurs, the Charles Lloyd group and Mwandishi.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: They want the foundation and they want to be able to — even if they’re not playing with the time per se or even the fills or whatever, they want the foundation for them to do their thing. And that’s a big ask I think. But it’s an interesting phenomenon because what Cecil’s basically saying is even though I do all that other stuff, you know, I do this because this is what works in that situation. You know? But Cecil could be all over the place, but he can also just be [hand motion steady beats] if that’s what the material calls for. You know? He does it. So that’s, I mean, and that’s another thing I love about those guys. I like these guys. Is they’ve all, and I’ve said this often, they’ve all been in the greatest bands that this music has shown. You know I used to — there was one tour where the record came out and we were on a good tour too and it was in June and there was like the basketball playoffs. And I kept using the San Antonio Spurs analogy because they were an older team but they were a team and they played well together. And I was like see — we’re the Spurs. See they were all great players but they all know roles. They don’t play the role all the time but they know how to make a great band. They’ve been a component in a great band. That doesn’t just happen, you’ve got to — I don’t want to say you’ve got to know your players, you know you have a role. You can still be the best musician you can be and play a role. It doesn’t have to be a restricting thing and it makes the band the band. I mean Cecil knows that from Charles Lloyd with Jack DeJohnette and Keith Jarrett. You know Eddie Henderson and Billy Hart know that from Mwandishi with Herbie Hancock. They basically said look, Herbie just made everything sound right. But you know, so those were great bands. They were all like bought into the system I mean you know certainly there was I don’t want to say “controversy” — you know there were some ruffled feathers here and there. But they all bought into the band. And you don’t really see that mentality too much anymore you know. You see cliques maybe but I don’t know if you see bands that much. I mean Jason Moran has kept his band together for a long time and it’s admirable and it certainly paid off, those guys are great. And some guys, like young guys, like Immanuel Wilkins has just kept his band together for a couple of years now and he’s starting to get out there and play. I don’t think he’ll be an interview but he’s going to do some really interesting stuff. He’s going to keep fresh. You know I’m going to go with fresh. I like fresh.
